analysis.title: Building resilience for 2027 (UBS House View - Daily EMEA)
key_insights: UBS CIO launched its Year Ahead 2027 outlook, 'Sustaining resilience'. The central message is to take risk more deliberately rather than retreat from markets: put excess cash to work, address portfolio concentration, rebalance toward fixed income and add differentiated return drivers.

UBS downgraded global equities from Attractive to Neutral after a multi-year bull run. It cites elevated expectations, index concentration and uncertainty around the AI investment cycle, while earnings forecasts stay constructive.
Asset class ranking for 2027: most favorable risk-reward in bonds and commodities, followed by equities, with cash as the least preferred asset class.

Global AI-related investment is expected to rise from USD 1.0 trillion in 2026 to USD 1.5 trillion in 2028. Cumulative US technology investment could approach USD 5.0 trillion by then, and revenues probably need to reach at least USD 1.5 trillion by 2030 for an adequate return.

AI risks named: competition, price cuts, costly monetization, open-weight models, harder external financing, market concentration, regulatory and company-specific risks. Not every company may reap the rewards.
The top 10 S&P 500 firms, most of them AI-exposed, make up 39% of the index. UBS says the market may start to apply a lower multiple to future earnings to account for rising risks.

UBS advises refocusing equity exposure and diversifying away from concentrated technology exposure. The Eurozone is the preferred equity market, with forecast 2027 earnings growth of 15%, comparable with the S&P 500 but from a lower starting valuation. It favors industrials and health care, and equal-weight strategies to reduce tech concentration.
Since the start of June the equal-weighted S&P 500 has outperformed the cap-weighted index by around 7 percentage points.

Bonds: elevated starting yields give income and a cushion against rising rates. UBS sees the best return opportunity within fixed income in emerging market and high yield bonds, and favors intermediate duration (maturities of about two to 10 years).
US high yield looks resilient: 60% of the market is rated BB, expected defaults are around 2%, and only 3% matures over the next year.

Gold upgraded to Attractive. Structural demand and an eventual easing in real yields should support a recovery toward USD 5,000 an ounce by December 2027. Oil should stay supported in the first half of 2027, and copper is the preferred industrial metal on electrification, power networks, data centers and AI demand.

Sterling is the preferred G10 carry currency. Selected emerging market currencies may benefit from high yields and contained volatility. Favored alternatives: dispersion-focused hedge funds, operationally focused private equity and secondaries, and infrastructure with visible cash flows.

Risk scenario: sticky inflation, elevated government debt and geopolitical risks could push bond yields higher and equities lower. Easing inflation is otherwise expected to allow yields to decline modestly later in 2027.

Today's calendar: FOMC minutes and commentary from Barr, Williams and Kashkari, EU and UK October CPI, US housing data and crude inventories, and Lagarde at the DealBook Summit. A UBS video segment is titled '25bps or 50bps Fed hike in December?'.
